observations: Photo 0: a used automotive alternator, dusty, no visible brand or part-number markings.
Photo 1: underside view of the same or a similar alternator, mounting ears visible, no legible markings.
Photo 2: side view with pulley and serpentine belt grooves, no stamped numbers or labels visible.
No vehicle make, engine code, or OEM part number is readable in any of the three photos.
Surface shows dirt, light corrosion, and wear consistent with a used/removed part; no packaging, invoice, or shipping label is shown to support the 'direct from Belgium' claim.

claims.evidence: No shipping label, customs tag, or import paperwork shown in any photo.
No bench-test clip, multimeter reading, or video of it spinning/charging is shown.
No audio/video of the pulley or rotor running is provided.
Mileage is not a property visible or verifiable from an alternator alone.
No close-up of seals, screws, or casing joints to confirm it hasn't been disassembled.

risks.risk: Unknown vehicle/engine fitment, which drives most of the price difference between comparables (Camry vs C300 vs M278).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped part number/OEM code on the alternator body, or the seller stating exact car make/model/engine it was pulled from.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be matched to any specific comparable; price range indeterminate

risks.risk: Electrical function (charging output, bearing noise, brush wear) cannot be confirmed from static photos.
risks.proof: A video of the alternator spinning on a bench test rig showing voltage output and no abnormal noise.

risks.risk: Internal condition (brushes, rotor windings, bearings) hidden by casing.
risks.proof: Photo of the alternator opened or a bench-test readout.
risks.if_unproven: priced as worst case / needing rebuild

risks.risk: Origin/import claim ('Tokunbo from Belgium') cannot be confirmed, which is sometimes used to justify inflated pricing.
risks.proof: Photo of shipping carton, customs documents, or container manifest.
risks.if_unproven: treated as ordinary used/local-market part, no import premium

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the stamped part number or OEM code on the alternator housing.
Seller to state the exact car make, model, year, and engine it was removed from.
A short video of the alternator being bench-tested (spinning with voltage reading).
Photo of any shipping/import documentation if the Belgium origin claim is to be relied on.
response.reason: The photos show a generic used alternator with no visible part number or vehicle fitment, so it cannot be matched to any of the listed comparables (which span very different vehicles and price tiers) without that information.
